items.question: Per Sect. 4.2.4, how much excess fuel above maximum gross mass can be taken on board for ground pre-flight checks with engines running?
options: Up to 20 kg
Up to 50 kg
No excess fuel is permitted at any time
Up to 100 kg
items.explanation: Sect. 4.2.4: for pre-flight checks and preparations on ground with engines running, fuel up to 20 kg in excess of maximum gross mass can be taken on board (idle fuel burn ~1.7 kg/min both engines). The pilot must still ensure takeoff mass does not exceed the maximum gross mass.

items.question: Per the caution in Sect. 4.2.3, what must never be done regarding the mission database (HTAWS, DMAP, SVS)?
options: Never load or swap the mission database in flight, as this could lead to loss of the SVS image
Never check database expiry before flight
Never use the DATAB pushbutton on the VMS/SYST page
Never install more than one database version per flight
items.explanation: Sect. 4.2.3 caution: loading or swapping the mission database in flight could lead to loss of the SVS image — never load or swap the mission database in flight.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.4.1.1, how frequently must the fire protection test (TEST FIRE 1/2) be performed?
options: At least once a day
Before every single flight, regardless of frequency
Once a week
Only after maintenance work on the fire system
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.1 note: the fire protection check must be performed at least once a day, testing both FIRE 1 and FIRE 2 systems.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.4.1.1, what minimum battery voltage should be confirmed on the VMS page during the pre-start check?
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.1: during the pre-start check, the VMS page volt reading should be checked as ≥23.5 V. If ELEC OVERLIMIT appears during engine start, the same 23.5 V threshold is used to determine if starting is still permitted.

items.question: Per the caution in Sect. 4.4.1.2, what should immediately abort the engine start sequence if ignition does not occur within a certain time?
options: 30 seconds with no TOT rise
10 seconds with no TOT rise
60 seconds with no TOT rise
90 seconds with no TOT rise
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 caution: immediately abort the start if ignition does not occur within 30 seconds (no TOT rise), if TOT reaches 840°C and the automatic stop function activates, if oil pressure indications are absent, or if N2/NR needles are unmatched at stabilized ground idle.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.4.1.2, at approximately what N1 value does the STARTER ON indication extinguish during a normal engine start?
options: Approximately 60% N1
Approximately 30% N1
Approximately 80% N1
Approximately 100% N1
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2: at approximately 60% N1, the STARTER ON indication (FND ML) and the START label (VMS page) extinguish; N2/NR should read approximately 78% in IDLE mode, matched.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.4.1.2 (Hydraulic check), what caution applies during this daily check regarding the mast moment?
options: Mast moment limits must be observed during the hydraulic check
Mast moment indication is automatically disabled during the check
The hydraulic check must never be performed with rotor turning
TEST HYD sw may be used freely during flight for this check
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 caution: the TEST HYD sw must not be operated during flight, and mast moment limits must be observed during the hydraulic check (performed at least once a day, on ground, checking SYS1 and SYS2 individually).

items.question: Per Sect. 4.4.1.3, why should the pilot avoid disconnecting the EPU later on during the pre-flight procedure rather than right after the second engine start?
options: It can cause systems and the AFCS to disengage, requiring them to be re-engaged before takeoff
It will trigger an unrecoverable ELEC OVERLIMIT fault
It permanently disables the standby battery
It has no operational effect and is purely a matter of preference
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.3 note: disconnecting the EPU later in the pre-flight procedure can cause systems and the AFCS to disengage; in that case they must be re-engaged before takeoff.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.4.1.3 (AFCS/Avionics Pre-flight Test), when must this test be performed, per the note?
options: Before each IFR flight; at least once a day before VFR flights
Only once per week, regardless of flight rules
Only after maintenance actions
Only for the first flight after a cold start below -30°C
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.3 note: the AFCS/Avionics pre-flight test must be performed before each IFR flight; before VFR flights, it must be performed at least once a day.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.4.1.3, the AFCS/Avionics pre-flight test should not be started until the main gearbox oil temperature is above what value?
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.3 note: do not start the AFCS/Avionics pre-flight test until the MGB oil temperature is above -10°C; in very cold conditions the yaw trim may fail the P-FLT TEST.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.5.1.1, the quick start-up procedure must NOT be used if which of the following applies?
options: More than 12 hours have passed since completion of the standard and additional pre-flight checks
The OAT is above +35°C
Only one pilot is operating the aircraft
The aircraft was refueled since the pre-flight checks
items.explanation: Sect. 4.5.1.1 caution: do not use the quick start-up procedure if the helicopter was left unattended, its settings/configuration were changed, or more than 12 hours have passed since the standard and additional pre-flight checks were completed.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.7 (Takeoff check), what N2/NR value must be confirmed during the hover check?
options: 101% or greater
95% or greater
85% or greater
110% or greater
items.explanation: Sect. 4.7: during the takeoff check, hover flight is performed and N2/NR is checked to be ≥101%, FLI checked for AEO indication, and hover power noted (blue line position on FLI) at 4 ft skid height.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.8 (Takeoff), what skid height is used for the hover before beginning acceleration and climb?
options: 4 ft
10 ft
2 ft
8 ft
items.explanation: Sect. 4.8: takeoff is performed from a hover at 4 ft skid height; acceleration begins with nose-down pitch and a smooth power increase (hover power plus 0.5-1.0 FLI, without exceeding TOP).

items.question: Per the recommended slope takeoff procedure in Sect. 4.8, what is the first AFCS-related action?
options: Press the A.TRIM sw to select A.TRIM OFF (DSAS mode)
Engage the backup SAS
Disengage both AP1 and AP2
Select GTC mode on the collective
items.explanation: Sect. 4.8: the recommended slope takeoff procedure begins by pressing the A.TRIM sw to select A.TRIM OFF (DSAS mode displayed on FND), then gently increasing collective to approximately 30% TQ before lifting off.

items.question: Per the recommended landing procedure in Sect. 4.10, what approach parameters should be targeted at 100 ft?
options: 40 KIAS with a rate of descent of not more than 500 ft/min
60 KIAS with a rate of descent of not more than 1000 ft/min
20 KIAS with a rate of descent of not more than 200 ft/min
80 KIAS with no rate-of-descent restriction
items.explanation: Sect. 4.10: the approach is initiated to arrive at 100 ft with a speed of 40 KIAS and a rate of descent of not more than 500 ft/min, then gradually slowing to 30 KIAS at 50 ft before proceeding into ground cushion.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.11 (Engine shutdown), the rotor brake may be applied once NR has decreased below what value?
options: 50% NR
80% NR
30% NR
70% NR
items.explanation: Sect. 4.11: after both ENG MAIN sw's are set OFF and TOT/N1 are monitored decreasing, the rotor brake (if required) may be applied below 50% NR.

items.question: Per the caution in Sect. 4.12.1 (Flight controls), what is prohibited during ground operations with the rotor turning?
options: Extreme cyclic stick displacements; only minimum control movements (less than 3 cm from neutral) are allowed for functional tests
Any movement of the cyclic stick whatsoever
Applying the rotor brake at any NR value
Selecting FND format on the MFDs
items.explanation: Sect. 4.12.1 caution: avoid extreme cyclic stick displacements when on ground with rotor turning; the cyclic must remain neutral and collective full down, except minimum control movements (less than 3 cm from neutral) for functional test purposes.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.12.2, what is the recommended maximum rate of descent during HOGE or low speed flight (up to 20 KIAS)?
options: Less than 500 ft/min
Less than 1000 ft/min
Less than 200 ft/min
Less than 1500 ft/min
items.explanation: Sect. 4.12.2: any descent during hover or low speed flight (up to 20 KIAS) should be performed with a descent rate of less than 500 ft/min, to avoid inadvertent entry into vortex ring state.

items.question: Per the caution in Sect. 4.13, when using altitude constrained legs, what must be true of the baro setting?
options: It must be identical on MFD1 and MFD2, and re-synchronized whenever changed
It only needs to be set on MFD1
It automatically synchronizes and needs no crew action
It is irrelevant for altitude constrained legs
items.explanation: Sect. 4.13 caution: when using altitude constrained legs, the baro setting must be identical on MFD1 and MFD2; the crew must remember to synchronize it whenever it is changed.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.13.3.1 (OBS navigation), what effect does selecting OBS have on automatic waypoint sequencing?
options: Automatic leg sequencing is suspended (SUSP appears on FND/NAVD)
It has no effect on sequencing, only on displayed course
It permanently disables sequencing until the flight plan is deleted
It forces immediate sequencing to the next waypoint
items.explanation: Sect. 4.13.3.1: the OBS function allows selecting a desired course to/from a waypoint and prevents the FMS from sequencing to the next waypoint — automatic leg sequencing is suspended, indicated by SUSP on FND/NAVD.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.13.4.2 (ILS approach), what is the minimum localizer interception distance, and within what deviation will LOC/GS capture automatically occur?
options: Minimum 4 NM interception distance; automatic capture within 2 dots (LOC) and 0.5 dots (GS)
Minimum 10 NM interception distance; automatic capture within 5 dots (LOC) and 2 dots (GS)
Minimum 2 NM interception distance; automatic capture within 1 dot (LOC) and 0.25 dots (GS)
There is no minimum interception distance specified
items.explanation: Sect. 4.13.4.2: minimum LOC interception distance is 4 NM; capturing of LOC and GS occurs automatically when the aircraft is within 2 dots (LOC) and 0.5 dots (GS).

items.question: Per Sect. 4.13.4.3 (LNAV or LP approach), if LP or LP+V does not appear but LNAV is indicated (e.g. due to loss of SBAS), what should the crew do?
options: Perform an approach using LNAV minima, adjusting DA/DH accordingly
Abort the approach entirely; no fallback is permitted
Continue using the original LP minima regardless
Switch immediately to an ILS approach instead
items.explanation: Sect. 4.13.4.3: if LNAV, LNAV+V, LP, or LP+V do not appear (GPS degradation), perform a missed approach; if LP/LP+V specifically don't appear but LNAV is shown (SBAS loss), perform the approach using LNAV minima with adjusted DA/DH.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.13.4.4 (LPV or LNAV/VNAV approach), if the autopilot IAS mode is engaged, to what maximum rate of descent will it automatically adjust the IAS during the approach?
options: 1000 ft/min
500 ft/min
1500 ft/min
2000 ft/min
items.explanation: Sect. 4.13.4.4 note: if the autopilot IAS mode is engaged during an LPV/LNAV-VNAV approach, it will automatically adjust IAS to achieve a maximum rate of descent of 1000 ft/min; the pilot may further reduce IAS but not increase it above that limit.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.13.4.5 (Missed approach, GPS approaches only), what does pushing the GA pb on the collective do to the autopilot NAV mode?
options: The autopilot remains coupled on NAV mode with automatic waypoint sequencing provided
It fully disengages the autopilot, requiring manual flight through the missed approach
It switches the autopilot to HOVER mode automatically
It has no effect on NAV mode, only on vertical guidance
items.explanation: Sect. 4.13.4.5 note: when using the GA pb on the collective to initiate a missed approach, the autopilot remains coupled on the NAV mode and automatic waypoint sequencing is provided.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.14.1, how long does the HTAWS self-test take after power-on, indicated by 'HTAWS TEST' on the FND?
options: About 2 minutes
About 30 seconds
About 10 minutes
About 5 minutes
items.explanation: Sect. 4.14.1: after power on, HTAWS performs a self-test for about 2 minutes, indicated by the HTAWS TEST label on the FND.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.14.2, after the HTAWS audio is manually inhibited (MUTE), how long until it is automatically re-activated?
options: After 5 minutes
After 30 minutes
After 1 minute
It remains inhibited until manually reactivated only
items.explanation: Sect. 4.14.2: HTAWS audio warnings can be inhibited via MUTE (held for 2 seconds); after 5 minutes, the audio is automatically re-activated and TAWS MUTE disappears from the master list.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.15.1 (AHRS free steering / DG mode), what caution applies to HDG1 and HDG2 settings when using DG mode?
options: HDG1 and HDG2 must be set to the same value (±7°) within one minute
HDG1 and HDG2 can be set to any independent values with no time limit
Only HDG1 needs to be set; HDG2 auto-syncs after landing
DG mode is only usable if both AHRS units have already failed
items.explanation: Sect. 4.15.1 caution: to avoid discrepancy indications and automatic deselection of heading sources, HDG1 and HDG2 must be set to the same value (±7°) within one minute; prolonged operation (>10 min) with one AHRS in MAG and the other in DG mode should be avoided.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.17.3 (Maximum ventilation / cooling), what is done with the BLD HTG rheostat?
options: Set to OFF
Set to MAX
Set to 40%
It is not part of this procedure
items.explanation: Sect. 4.17.3: for maximum ventilation/cooling, the BLD HTG rheostat is set OFF, VENTILATION CKPT rheostat set to HI, VENTILATION PAX sw ON, all pax vent nozzles opened, and airspeed increased if possible.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.17.5, how is recirculated air selected to prevent outside air (e.g. sand/dust) from entering the ventilation system?
options: Pull the PUSH FOR AIR lever
Push the PUSH FOR AIR lever
Set BLD HTG rheostat to MAX
Switch VENTILATION PAX sw to OFF only
items.explanation: Sect. 4.17.5: to select recirculated air (e.g. during landings in sand/dust or very cold conditions), pull the PUSH FOR AIR lever.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.18.1 (Cold weather, MGB temperature below -30°C), is it necessary to start both engines to warm up the MGB and hydraulic system?
options: No, starting only one engine is sufficient to warm up the MGB and hydraulic system
Yes, both engines must always be started simultaneously
No engine start is required; an external heater must be used instead
Only the auxiliary power unit can perform this warm-up
items.explanation: Sect. 4.18.1 note: starting only one engine is sufficient to warm up the MGB and hydraulic system when MGB temperature is below -30°C; the engine is shut down once MGB oil temperature exceeds -10°C.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.19, which of the four (semi-)automatic pre-flight test phases is initiated manually by the crew BEFORE engine start?
options: Lamp test
Power-up test
Start-up test
Pre-flight test
items.explanation: Sect. 4.19: the power-up test launches automatically when both AMCs power up; the lamp test is initiated by the crew before engine start; the start-up test launches automatically when one engine starts; the pre-flight test is initiated by the crew once both engines are running and avionics master switches are on.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.19, what symbol appears above the master list area to remind the crew that a completed test phase ended with failure messages?
options: An encircled (T)
A flashing red X
A yellow triangle
The letters 'FAIL' in red
items.explanation: Sect. 4.19: when the next test phase begins, messages from the previous phase are removed from the master list, but an encircled (T) is displayed above the master list area as a reminder that a test phase ended with failure messages (viewable anytime on the CT page).

items.question: Per Sect. 4.19.1, if FADEC1 SIGNAL FAIL or SIGNAL FAIL FADEC2 appears during the power-up test, what is the required action?
options: Abort mission — no information is being received from the FADECs
Consult MEL/MMEL for VFR flight only
Continue flight, this fault clears itself after start-up test
Reset the FADEC using the EMER sw
items.explanation: Sect. 4.19.1: FADEC1 SIGNAL FAIL / SIGNAL FAIL FADEC2 during the power-up test means no information is being received from the FADECs — the required action is to abort the mission.

items.question: Per Sect. 4.19.4 (Pre-flight test), how can the test be aborted if required?
options: Push the AP/BKUP CUT switch twice, which will display APi TST ABORTED
Push the TEST sw to LAMP position
Cycle the BAT MSTR switch OFF and back ON
There is no way to abort the pre-flight test once started
items.explanation: Sect. 4.19.4: if required, the pre-flight test can be aborted by pushing the AP/BKUP CUT switch twice, at which point APi TST ABORTED will appear.
